pillar_reactions.evidence: Tied the month-one form phase directly to his own stated fear: 'Yeah, I like that. Cause like, I don't want to, if you're like, let's start doing really high weight, complex movement right out of the gate... you're doing the foundational build, mastering the movement... and then working up the intensity and working up the weight that you get better results that way as well.'

Agreed with the framing and volunteered his own gap rather than pushing back: 'I would say my biggest opportunity for my diet is probably more eating... I'll go just straight up eight to 10 hours, and I might have some water.' Earlier he had said 'that's kind of my philosophy already, so that's perfect.'

Asked how the mechanics actually work rather than reacting to the idea: 'How is it tracked? Is it in an app or is it like in like a diary type thing?' and 'and then it's a once a week check-in?' Then approved the shape of it: 'I like the data.'

anchors.note: Proposed label: free_self_directed_substitute. This is the sharpest version of the known script gap: the anchor is the brand's own free marketing, which is already producing results for him five days a week. He confirmed he stays regardless — 'I'll still be a subscriber though, either way' — so the paid offer has to beat a free product he already likes.

anchors.raw: I'm not like a professional trainer. You know, I just watch videos online. I'm like, I'm going to do that exercise.
anchors.note: Proposed label: self_admitted_capability_gap. The one genuinely supportive anchor in the call — he named the exact deficiency the product fixes. The rep never came back to it when the free-resources objection arrived.
